fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Moses says, “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One.” (Deuteronomy 6:4). He opens with the word Hear, so Israel is told to listen up. Later in this same sermon he says to serve Him only (Deuteronomy 6:13).

Nope, baker. Moses says “The LORD our God, the LORD is One.” (Deuteronomy 6:4). That verse doesn't mention anyone sharing a throne. A few verses later he says, “Fear the LORD your God, serve Him only…” (Deuteronomy 6:13). One LORD, and Him only.

Right, baker. “…all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.” (Deuteronomy 6:5). Moses names three things and puts the word all in front of every one. Heart, soul and strength, none held back.

Almost, friend, but Moses doesn't leave a piece out. He says to love the LORD your God “…with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.” (Deuteronomy 6:5). The word in front of heart, soul and strength is all, not most. Three things named, and each one gets the whole thing.

Some is a small word, friend, and Moses doesn't use it. He says “…with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength.” (Deuteronomy 6:5). Say it with me: ALL, ALL, ALL! Once for the heart, once for the soul, once for the strength.

Good thought, but that's not what the verse says. Moses says “…you shall teach them diligently to your children…” (Deuteronomy 6:7). He goes on to say to speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road. Neighbors aren't named in that verse, friend.

Yep. Moses says “Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates.” (Deuteronomy 6:9). The doorposts of the houses and the gates are the spots he names. Walk past one of those, baker, and there the words are.

That's right, baker. Moses says the land has “…wells that you did not dig, and with vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant…” (Deuteronomy 6:11). Somebody else did the digging and the planting. And Israel is the one who gets to enjoy them.

Not on this list, baker. Moses names “…houses full of every good thing with which you did not fill them, with wells that you did not dig, and with vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant…” (Deuteronomy 6:11). Houses, wells, vineyards and olive groves. Not one chariot in the lineup.

It's true, friend. Moses says “Fear the LORD your God, serve Him only, and take your oaths in His name.” (Deuteronomy 6:13). Fear, serve and swear, and every one of them points at the LORD. Moses packed a whole lot into one verse.

That's the word, baker. “Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah.” (Deuteronomy 6:16). Massah is a place Israel knew, and Moses points back to it. That's the whole warning, right there in one verse.

Close, but flee isn't the word. Moses says “Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah.” (Deuteronomy 6:16). The warning is about testing the LORD, and he points back to Massah, a place Israel knew. Fleeing isn't mentioned in that verse, friend.

Not quite, baker. Moses says “Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah.” (Deuteronomy 6:16). The verse is about testing, and it points back to Massah, where they tested Him. Cursing doesn't show up in it.

That's it. Moses says to do what is right and good “…so that it may be well with you and that you may enter and possess the good land…” (Deuteronomy 6:18). It's the good land the LORD swore to give their fathers. That's the reason Moses gives, baker.

Not what Moses says, baker. He says to do what is right and good “…so that it may be well with you and that you may enter and possess the good land…” (Deuteronomy 6:18). Then he speaks of “…driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said.” (Deuteronomy 6:19). Peace with their enemies isn't in these verses.

Yep. Moses speaks of “…driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said.” (Deuteronomy 6:19). That comes right after he talks about entering and possessing the good land. He says it plainly, baker.

Moses actually says it, friend. He speaks of “…driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has said.” (Deuteronomy 6:19). That follows the possessing of the good land in the verse before. So as he describes it, taking the land includes driving out their enemies, and the answer is true.

That's the word, baker. “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt…” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was Egypt's king. That's how the answer to the son begins, and then it goes on to say the LORD brought them out with a mighty hand.

Guests would've been a different story, friend. But Moses says “We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt…” (Deuteronomy 6:21). Pharaoh was Egypt's king. The answer to the son starts there, and then it tells how the LORD brought them out.
